title: New UFO Files disclosure reveals six flying objects over the Middle East
excerpt: Pentagon has released a new batch of UFO files where six flying objects were reportedly spotted over the Middle East. Fox News reported that the White House published three clips of unidentified flying objects from three different timelines.
content:
Rajarshi Deb

Updated Fri, September 18, 2026 at 2:56 PM UTC

Pentagon has released a new batch of UFO files where six flying objects were reportedly spotted over the Middle East. Fox News reported that the White House published three clips of unidentified flying objects from three different timelines.

According to the news outlet, the third footage, released last year, revealed that six flying objects were spotted over the Middle East, but no one could say anything about the destination of those objects.

Peter Doocy joined Fox News live from the White House and revealed these three exclusive footages. Doocy shared that he was summoned to an office in the West Wing yesterday for a private briefing about these files.

Continue reading more about the story.

Fresh UFO files report six mysterious objects over the Middle East

As per Fox News, the White House has unveiled newly declassified UFO documents about six unidentified flying objects observed over the Middle East. Peter Doocy said,

"We have a third clip taken by a drone over the Middle East last year. It shows six objects flying in formation, destination unknown."

The video showed a mysterious orb racing across a residential neighborhood in the Middle East. The investigators labeled the case as unresolved and acknowledged that they could not confidently determine the identity of the object.

The third clip reportedly showed a round object moving quickly above a crowded area. Officials stated that the object showed strange features that could not be explained with the available data.

The case summary stated that analysts could not confirm if the object was a drone, balloon, aircraft, or any other known aerial vehicle. Because of this, the sighting is still marked as undetermined. Authorities explained that an uncertain case should not be taken as proof of alien life and further stressed that "unresolved" only means there is not enough information to reach a clear conclusion.

DIA is investigating the case

Peter Doocy mentioned that according to a declassified expense report, the Defense Intelligence Agency spent $22 million to investigate long-running claims linked to Skinwalker Ranch, including reports of strange objects in the sky, UFOs, and UAPs.

The report was a line‑by‑line record of how the money was used. In 2008, Harry Reid secured the funding to carry out the investigation. Officials now say that senior White House staff cannot locate any copy of those records.
